#### 1. fibrosis of extraocular muscles, congenital, 3A, with or without extraocular involvement  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:20772)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic TUBB3 variant (HP:0001244) —DISRUPTS→ TUBB3 (HGNC:12011); TUBB3 (HGNC:12011) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule dynamics and neuronal development (GO:0007017); Microtubule dynamics and neuronal development (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles (HP:0000524); Microtubule dynamics and neuronal development (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles (HP:0000524); Microtubule dynamics and neuronal development (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles (HP:0000524). Loss-of-function mutations in TUBB3 disrupt microtubule dynamics and neuronal development, leading to congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in TUBB3 with a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, the absence of mutations in TUBB3 in a significant proportion of patients with MONDO:0013541 would also weaken this hypothesis, suggesting locus heterogeneity.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TUBB3 in these two conditions could lead to the development of targeted therapies that aim to restore normal microtubule function, potentially benefiting patients with both MONDO:0013541 and congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles, 3A.
